name: SteeringBehaviors
src_typeComment: Classic steering-behavior math (Reynolds-style): each function returns a STEERING FORCE to add to current velocity, not a position or a velocity itself. Plain static math, not tied to any specific mover — SteeringAgent is the ready-to-drop-in MonoBehaviour that actually applies these; use these functions directly if you're driving movement some other way (Rigidbody, CharacterController, NavMesh).

src_members.sig: public static Vector3 Seek(Vector3 position, Vector3 velocity, Vector3 target, float maxSpeed, float maxForce)
src_members.name: Seek
src_members.comment: Steers straight toward the target at full speed.

src_members.sig: public static Vector3 Flee(Vector3 position, Vector3 velocity, Vector3 target, float maxSpeed, float maxForce)
src_members.name: Flee
src_members.comment: Steers straight away from the target at full speed — Seek with the desired direction flipped.

src_members.id: Arrive(Vector3, Vector3, Vector3, float, float, float)
src_members.sig: public static Vector3 Arrive(Vector3 position, Vector3 velocity, Vector3 target, float maxSpeed, float maxForce, float slowRadius)
src_members.name: Arrive
src_members.comment: Like Seek, but decelerates smoothly on approach instead of overshooting and correcting — use this for "move to and stop at" rather than "chase forever" (racing AI slowing into a waypoint, an NPC walking up to a chair).

src_members.id: Wander(Vector3, Vector3, ref float, float, float)
src_members.sig: public static Vector3 Wander(Vector3 position, Vector3 velocity, ref float wanderAngle, float maxSpeed, float maxForce,
src_members.name: Wander
src_members.comment: Wanders with a smoothly-changing random direction instead of jittering every frame. `wanderAngle` is caller-owned state (a float you keep between calls, e.g. a field on your MonoBehaviour) — this function reads and updates it in place, which is what makes the wander direction drift smoothly over time instead of snapping to a new random direction each call.

src_members.id: Flock(Vector3, Vector3, IReadOnlyList<(Vector3 position, Vector3 velocity)>)
src_members.sig: public static Vector3 Flock(Vector3 position, Vector3 velocity, IReadOnlyList<(Vector3 position, Vector3 velocity)> neighbors,
src_members.name: Flock
src_members.comment: Reynolds-style flocking/boids: blends three rules into one steering force — separation (push away from nearby flockmates so they don't overlap), alignment (match their average heading), and cohesion (drift toward their average position, reusing Seek). `neighbors` is caller-gathered (e.g. via Physics.OverlapSphere against other flocking agents) rather than looked up here, so this stays plain math with no dependency on how neighbors are actually found.
